Authorization V3 PR #1067 / head 24f02e36310ce083f5327a78728cd4ed4f358520 is frozen RED on its delegated supersession schema. Authorization V4 PR #1068 / head 3d56f8d9079a5ba6ea2023f1035a60bdb1fe7436 proved that supersession repair GREEN but is frozen RED because its otherwise valid OSS-first evidence omitted required retireOrAvoid. V5 preserves the exact V4 implementation intent and scope, adds only the missing duplicate-path retirement/avoidance evidence, re-derives the proven V2 cleanup/retry repair from trusted main, constrains npm's own fetch budget strictly inside the outer hard deadline, and makes audit-result shape fail closed without changing XState pinning, audit thresholds, supply-chain authority, workflows, dependencies, or upstream test selection.

supersedes.reason: V2 authorized the now-frozen implementation head e87b184ef679e403c73ae71499a86bded955f9f6; V5 replaces that implementation authority for the distinct npm-audit execution-authority root while preserving V2 and the unmerged V3/V4 authorization attempts as immutable historical evidence.

rootCause.directFailure: Frozen run 33827101178 proved two bounded outer NPM_AUDIT retries both hit the 120000ms hard timeout on Ubuntu and Windows with empty stdout/stderr; Windows runner cleanup then terminated an orphan node process. This means outer retry/cleanup is working but npm's own network/process lifetime is not bounded below repository governance.
rootCause.sameRootSurface: verify-wp-b-xstate-package.js owns the npm audit command, audit transport budget, result parsing and package scratch lifecycle; verify-wp-b-xstate-upstream.js owns the outer scratch lifecycle that must preserve the already-proven V2 cleanup authority; xstateUpstreamEvidenceGate.test.js owns deterministic regressions for the same timeout/audit authority.
rootCause.requiredRepair: Re-derive the V2 bounded whole-audit retry and Node built-in recursive cleanup on fresh trusted main. Add explicit npm CLI fetch retry/timeout configuration whose internal network deadline is strictly lower than the existing 120000ms outer NPM_AUDIT timeout, using npm's existing config surface rather than a new HTTP client or supervisor. Require a structurally valid npm audit report with numeric vulnerability metadata; parseable transport/error JSON or missing/invalid metadata must fail closed. Preserve real npm audit, existing high/critical policy, all non-audit package checks and the real upstream pnpm test:core command.

causalEvidence.ubuntuFailure: Two governed NPM_AUDIT attempts each reached 120000ms and final error remained WP_B_UPSTREAM_COMMAND_TIMEOUT; stdout/stderr empty.
causalEvidence.windowsFailure: Two governed NPM_AUDIT attempts each reached 120000ms and final error remained WP_B_UPSTREAM_COMMAND_TIMEOUT; runner cleanup later terminated orphan node.

requiredBehavior: Preserve exact XState xstate@5.32.5, upstream tag/commit, tarball digests, MIT license and supply-chain authority.
Preserve real npm audit --omit=dev --json evidence and existing high/critical vulnerability rejection semantics.
Preserve the repository outer NPM_AUDIT hard timeout at 120000ms per attempt and the fixed two-attempt whole-audit cap proven in V2.

Use npm's native fetch-timeout/fetch-retry configuration to ensure npm's own registry request budget terminates before the repository outer timeout; no custom HTTP client, no new dependency and no unbounded wait.

A parseable npm JSON payload is not sufficient by itself: metadata.vulnerabilities must exist with finite non-negative numeric info/low/moderate/high/critical/total counts or the audit result fails closed.
Transport/error JSON, malformed audit output, rate limits, tool failures and command execution failures must never become zero-vulnerability success.
Retain Node built-in recursive fs.rmSync maxRetries/retryDelay for all package/tag/outer upstream owned scratch and preserve the primary verification error when cleanup also fails.
Keep corepack pnpm install/test:core selection and all physical artifact checks unchanged.
